ocr.notes: minor slips: 'where he calls himself' is 'whereof he calleth himself'; 'work me' is 'mark me'; 'fighter' is 'fightist'; 'say any more against me' is 'agin me'; dialect 'foight'/'whoame' normalized

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Republican interviewed Tom Allen at his Washington Avenue saloon, where he called the bill against prize-fighting unnecessary yet agreed the ring was so corrupt that a fair fight was impossible.

metadata.notes: page head reads THE ST. LOUIS REPUBLICAN, FRIDAY MORNING, FEBRUARY 20, 1874, page 8; interview took place 'yesterday'

facts.fact: Allen was interviewed at his saloon on Washington Avenue by the tunnel in St. Louis
Allen said the Missouri law against prize-fighting was unnecessary because fights were always held outside the state
facts.quote: I think it's unnecessary and uncalled for in this state.

facts.fact: Allen said the ring had become so corrupt that he sided with the legislature
facts.quote: I side with the legislature about this bill against prize-fighting. If it's got so that there can't be a fair fight, why, stop it.

facts.fact: Allen said his name had been put in the bill and denied being a refugee, saying he meant to stay in St. Louis
facts.quote: I'm no refugee; I can go back whenever I want to go. I'm a prize-fighter, and they can't say any more agin me than that. No man can ever say I've done wrong against him. I came here to live, and I'm going to stay here.

facts.fact: Allen said Arthur Chambers and Billy Edwards were coming to St. Louis about March 7 to give sparring exhibitions at Deagle's for a week, to test Mudd's bill

notes: Washington Avenue saloon is likely the 417 Washington Ave concert hall (facts 009/017), but no number is given
